To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cadherin Cad-6 is essential for normal kidney development.
Cad-6 mutant mice have fewer nephrons than normal mice and that these nephrons develop with a delay in epithelialization of the metanephros and fusion of the renal vesicle to the ureter.
Cad-6 mutant mice are viable and complete both early and later aspects of nephrogenic development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of kidney development, and how these mechanisms may be altered in disease states such as polycystic kidney disease.
the mechanisms that control the formation, maintenance, and repair of epithelial tissues, and we have used the kidney as a model system to address these issues.
the mechanisms of kidney development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cadherins, in particular the cadherin- 6, play an essential role as cell adhesion molecule in the formation of the renal vesicle and its fusion with the ureter.
the cadherin family plays an important role in kidney development and that the cadherins are important in the formation of a continuous epithelial tube.
cadherin- 6 plays a role in epithelialization of the nephron.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cad6 is essential for epithelial morphogenesis in the kidney, but it is not essential for the maintenance of the epithelial phenotype.
cadherin- 6 is required for the normal development and function of the kidney.
Cad-6 is essential for normal development of the metanephros.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cadherin- 6 is required for the formation of the renal vesicle and that the renal vesicle is required for nephrogenesis.
cadherin- 6 is important for the formation of the epithelial structures in the developing kidneys.
cadherins are essential for epithelial morphogenesis, and that the timing of cadherin expression is critical to this process.
